root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before vulnerable `luaD_pretailcall()` may let `checkstackGC(L, fsize)` re-enter Lua or raise, the reused `CallInfo` must still describe the caller frame rather than the callee `Proto *p` being moved down into `ci->func`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The selected root obligation is the pre-check ordering constraint on the reused tail-call frame. In the vulnerable original the move-down loop runs first, so the frame already resolves the callee when `checkstackGC()` can still fail. In the fixed original the same root event is reached with distinct caller and callee `Proto` pointers.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The frozen required assertion is violated on the vulnerable original at `tailcall_root_state` and is genuine on the fixed original at the same event, so no perturbation witness was needed.

nodes.state: On the crashing `luaG_getfuncline()` walk, the carried instruction index has advanced `basepc` to or past `f->sizelineinfo`, so the next `f->lineinfo[basepc]` load is the AddressSanitizer-reported out-of-bounds read.
`currentpc()` computes an instruction index outside the current `Proto`'s code range because `ci->u.l.savedpc` still belongs to the caller while `ci_func(ci)->p` already names the callee.

edges.relation: The out-of-range `pc` computed by `currentpc()` is passed unchanged into `luaG_getfuncline()` and drives the later `f->lineinfo[basepc]` walk.
The callee `Proto` exposed by the vulnerable pre-check frame rewrite is the same `ci_func(ci)->p` later consumed by `currentpc()` when it computes the invalid instruction index.
The caller `savedpc` snapshot taken by `savepc(ci)` in `OP_TAILCALL` is carried unchanged into `currentpc()`, where it is still paired with the rewritten callee `Proto`.
